plan_needed: Any Dropbox plan and any Claude plan that has directory connectors (Anthropic says Claude, Cowork, Claude Desktop and Claude mobile). Your organisation must allow the Dropbox app; on Claude Team or Enterprise an owner adds it first (see claude-owner-allows-dropbox).

steps.do: Click the add (+) icon in the search bar, then Add connectors.
steps.see: The connectors directory opens.

steps.do: Click the add (+) icon next to Dropbox (made by Dropbox, Anthropic verified).
steps.see: You're sent to Dropbox to sign in.

steps.do: Log in to the Dropbox account you want Claude to use.
steps.see: Dropbox lists the permissions Claude asks for: view and edit files and folders, sharing information and file requests, and view account information.

steps.do: Review the permissions and click Continue.
steps.see: You're returned to Claude with Dropbox connected.

steps.do: Click + (or type /), go to Connectors and switch Dropbox on.
steps.see: Claude can find, organise and share files and save text files to Dropbox, within your own Dropbox permissions.

desktop_alternative: In the Claude desktop app, in the Chat, Cowork or Code tab: Customize > Connectors > Add > Browse connectors, search for Dropbox, add it, log in and click Continue.

undo.see: Claude can no longer reach your Dropbox. Dropbox's Claude page doesn't give steps for the Dropbox side.

plan_needed: A paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise) and any Dropbox plan. Your organisation must allow the plugin.

steps.where: claude.ai, or the Claude desktop app (Chat, Cowork or Code tab)
steps.do: On claude.ai click Browse plugins. In the desktop app click Customize > Plugins > Add.
steps.see: The plugin directory.

steps.do: Search for Dropbox and add it.
steps.see: You may be asked to authorise Dropbox.

steps.do: Complete the Dropbox authorisation if prompted.
steps.see: The plugin is installed. Dropbox says it can organise files and folders, make share links and save text files.

plan_needed: Claude Team or Enterprise, owner role.

steps.do: Go to Connectors, click Add+ for Dropbox and save. (Anthropic's own path: Organization settings > Connectors > Browse connectors > Add to your team.)
steps.see: Dropbox is available to the team. Each person still signs in to their own Dropbox.

steps.do: Optionally set each Dropbox tool to Always allow, Needs approval or Blocked.
steps.see: Members can't override these settings.

steps.do: Open the more options menu next to Dropbox and choose Not available, Installed by Default, Available to Install or Required.
steps.see: The plugin's availability for your team changes. Anthropic's plugin page lists only Available to install, Installed by default and Required.

undo.do: Open the more options menu next to Dropbox and click Delete.
undo.see: The Dropbox connector is blocked for the team.

plan_needed: Any Dropbox plan. Neither Dropbox nor OpenAI names the ChatGPT plans; OpenAI says availability depends on plan, region and workspace settings, and some workspaces need admin approval.

steps.do: Click Plugins in the left sidebar.
steps.see: The plugin directory.

steps.do: Select Dropbox (developer: Dropbox) and click Install plugin.
steps.see: A prompt to sign in.

steps.do: Click Sign in with Dropbox.
steps.see: The Dropbox sign-in page.

steps.do: Log in. If you have paired personal and work accounts, choose the one to connect.
steps.see: Dropbox is connected. The exact approval screen wasn't in the docs we read.

steps.do: Enter @Dropbox in your prompt, or click the add button in the prompt box and choose Dropbox, then describe what you want.
steps.see: ChatGPT can find, summarise, organise, move, copy, delete, save and share. Dropbox says it asks permission before changing anything.

undo.do: Click your avatar (bottom left), then Settings > Apps. Click the arrow next to ChatGPT, then Disconnect.
undo.see: The connection is removed on the Dropbox side.

plan_needed: A Dash plan or Dash trial (team must be in the US, UK or Australia). OpenAI says availability depends on the plugin, your plan and workspace settings.

steps.do: Find the Dropbox Dash plugin (developer: Dropbox).
steps.see: The plugin's details.

steps.do: Install the plugin, then follow the prompts to review permissions and connect.
steps.see: Not described in detail in the pages we read.

steps.do: Type @ in the prompt field, select Dropbox Dash and ask a work question.
steps.see: Dash pulls in content from your connected work apps. It only uses content you're allowed to see in each app.

plan_needed: Any Dropbox plan and Microsoft Copilot with Cowork. Cowork for work accounts is generally available to Microsoft 365 Copilot tenants; Cowork for personal accounts is in preview. Your organisation might need to approve the plugin.

steps.where: copilot.com or the Copilot desktop app
steps.do: Log in to your Microsoft Copilot account.
steps.see: Copilot opens. Microsoft gives copilot.cloud.microsoft as the web address for Cowork on work accounts.

steps.do: Go to Copilot Cowork and click Customize in the left navigation bar.
steps.see: Plugins you can add.

steps.do: Search for Dropbox for Copilot. Click Install, then Connect.
steps.see: A Dropbox authorisation window.

steps.do: Log in to Dropbox and click Allow.
steps.see: Dropbox is connected to Cowork.

steps.do: Click New task and mention Dropbox in your prompt.
steps.see: Copilot can find, summarise and organise files, make shared links and save new text files up to 5 MB. Cowork asks before important actions.

undo.do: Click your avatar, then Settings > Apps. Click the arrow next to Copilot, then Disconnect.
undo.see: Copilot loses access to your Dropbox.

undo.do: Select + > Customize, find the plugin and select Remove from Cowork.
undo.see: The plugin is removed. Plugins your admin deployed can only be removed by the admin.

plan_needed: Dropbox Advanced or Enterprise, a Dropbox admin, and a Microsoft 365 admin.

steps.do: Select Create app. Give it a unique name, Scoped access and Full Dropbox access.
steps.see: A new Dropbox app.

steps.where: Dropbox App Console, OAuth 2.0 and Permissions tabs
steps.do: Add Microsoft's redirect address and the scopes Microsoft lists.
steps.see: The app is ready to authorise the connector.

steps.do: Copy the app key and app secret.
steps.see: The two values the Microsoft admin needs.

steps.do: Choose Copilot > Connectors, open the Gallery tab and choose Dropbox.
steps.see: The Dropbox connector setup page.

steps.do: Enter the app key and app secret. Optionally switch on Rollout to limited audience.
steps.see: Authentication is set up (OAuth 2.0 is required).

steps.do: Under access permissions choose Only people with access to this data source, then choose Create.
steps.see: Indexing starts straight away. Without this change the default makes every file anyone can open in Dropbox visible to all Microsoft 365 users in your tenant.

plan_needed: A personal Google account, aged 18 or over, in the US, with Keep Activity on. Not offered in Australia: Google lists it as US only. Work and school accounts aren't supported yet.

steps.do: Log in and click Settings.
steps.see: Gemini settings.

steps.do: Click Personal Intelligence, then Connected apps.
steps.see: Your connected apps.

steps.do: Click Other and switch Dropbox On.
steps.see: A permission prompt.

steps.do: Click Allow, then Continue. Click Agree and continue, then Allow.
steps.see: Dropbox is connected.

steps.do: Type @Dropbox in the prompt box and ask.
steps.see: Gemini can find, summarise, create, rename, move and delete files. You confirm deleting, sharing, permission changes and bulk actions.

undo.do: Click your avatar, then Settings > Apps. Click the arrow next to Gemini, then Disconnect.
undo.see: The connection is removed on the Dropbox side.

plan_needed: A Claude plan that allows custom connectors (Dropbox says 'select Claude plans'). Your Dropbox admin may control whether you can connect apps. The server is in beta.

steps.do: Go to Settings > Connectors and click Add custom connector.
steps.see: A form for the connector's name and address.

steps.do: Enter the name Dropbox MCP and the address https://mcp.dropbox.com/mcp, then click Add.
steps.see: The connector is added.

steps.do: Sign in to Dropbox when asked and approve the access.
steps.see: Claude can read, create, move, delete and share through the server's tools. Deleted items go to Deleted files.

plan_needed: ChatGPT Business, Enterprise or Edu for full MCP (Pro can connect read and fetch only). On Business only admins and owners can create these. The server is in beta.

steps.where: ChatGPT, Settings > Apps & Connectors > Advanced settings
steps.do: Dropbox's steps: toggle Developer mode on and click Confirm.
steps.see: OpenAI's current page says Enterprise and Edu users can add a custom MCP server from Plugins without turning on Developer Mode first.

steps.do: Click Create app. Enter the name Dropbox MCP and the address https://mcp.dropbox.com/mcp, and set Authentication to OAuth.
steps.see: A risk warning to acknowledge.

steps.do: Tick the acknowledgement box and click Create.
steps.see: You're asked to sign in to Dropbox.

steps.do: Complete the Dropbox sign-in and approve access.
steps.see: The Dropbox MCP tools are available in ChatGPT.

to: AI apps (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini and others)
plan_needed: Dropbox Standard, Business, Advanced, Business Plus or Enterprise, team admin.

steps.do: Under Products, open the dropdown beside Dropbox, click Settings and open the Integrations tab.
steps.see: The team's app settings and app list.

steps.do: Tick each app you want to block, then click Block.
steps.see: Blocked apps still appear in the App Center but can't be connected.

steps.do: Optionally open the dropdown next to Connecting registered integrations and select Block.
steps.see: New registered integrations are blocked by default.

note: Dropbox says blocking apps doesn't disconnect team members who are already connected.
